items.detail: The **S&P 500** fell about 2% to 7,175.83 Thursday, a sixth straight loss and its longest losing streak since 2024, while the Nasdaq sank 2.3% to 23,879.20.
items.why: Investors grew more worried that the AI boom is over, and Nvidia went from a 4.7% early gain to a loss.

items.detail: In its first day of trading, **Anthropic** closed at **$97.17**, 17% above its $83 IPO price but well below its $111.50 opening trade.
items.why: The broad tech selloff took back much of the early jump and kept the debut from lifting other AI stocks.

items.detail: The Dow dropped about **1,100 points**, or 2.2%, and only one of its 30 stocks closed higher, as more than 90% of S&P 500 members fell.
items.why: With traders all but certain of a December Fed hike, the AI selling spread to the rest of the market.

items.detail: Taiwan's stocks fell about 5% Friday and are on track for a **16% weekly drop**, the biggest since 1991, while South Korea's KOSPI slid about 4.7%.
items.why: Wall Street's AI reversal hit Asia's chipmakers hard, with SK Hynix and Samsung each down more than 5%.

items.detail: The **Sensex** opened down about 450 points Friday but recovered to 83,190.82 by late morning, while the Nifty climbed back above 25,550.
items.why: Banks and IT stocks led the recovery as foreign funds kept buying, which cushioned the hit from Asia's selloff.

items.detail: In the US, the **Russell 2000** gave back Wednesday's bounce, falling 2.2% to 2,655.11 Thursday, and is down 4.9% for the week.
items.why: Thursday's selloff was broad, and with a December Fed hike nearly certain, rate-sensitive small caps had little shelter.

items.detail: **Bitcoin** fell another 2.15% to $61,635 Thursday evening and briefly touched **$60,000**, before bouncing.
items.why: Spot bitcoin ETFs have lost more than $2.5 billion this month, and money leaving AI stocks went to cash, not crypto.

items.detail: **Ether** dipped as low as about $1,717 Thursday before steadying near **$1,760** Friday, still below the $1,800 level it lost earlier this week.
items.why: Bets on Fed hikes, higher Treasury yields and ETF outflows kept pressure on the coin.

items.detail: **Solana** held roughly flat at about **$72.75** Friday, down just 0.29% over 24 hours and still above last weekend's four-month low.
items.why: It moved sideways as bitcoin's bounce off $60,000 calmed the wider crypto market for now.

items.detail: **Gold** slid toward $3,525 Friday, a new 14-month low, and is heading for a weekly loss of about **9%**, its worst since March.
items.why: Traders now see a December Fed hike as about 97% likely, and some sold gold to raise cash during the AI selloff.

crossCuttingTheme: Doubts about the AI boom turned into a global selloff, and with a December Fed hike nearly certain, investors fled to cash, sinking US and Asian chip stocks, small caps, bitcoin and even gold together.
